subject: Intermittent fragmented streaming + WS negotiation timeouts — urgent escalation
messages:
From: Carlos Mendez <carlos.m@harmony.ai>
To: chloe_martin <chloe.martin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Harmony AI Support <support@harmony.ai>
Date: Fri, 29 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Fragmented stream + WS negotiation timeouts from Dedicated pool

Hi Chloe,

We started seeing a spike of 502/101 errors from clients connecting to our real-time inference route this morning (around 09:05 PST). The symptoms: partial token chunks appearing then a WS close with "101 switching protocols" followed by immediate reconnect attempts. Throughput drops ~30% during the window and p95 latency jumps from 120ms to ~1.4s.

Attached is a packet capture and a short trace we captured from the connector node. This is hitting your Dedicated pool in us-west-2 (pool id: ded-78). Can you confirm whether there were infra changes or known degradation? Our user-facing SLA is impacted and leadership is asking for an immediate mitigation.

Thanks,
Carlos
Senior Platform Engineer
Harmony AI

Attachments: packet_capture.pcap (pcap), trace_log_20260529.txt (txt)

From: chloe_martin <chloe.martin@redwood.ai>
To: Carlos Mendez <carlos.m@harmony.ai>
Cc: sean_gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>, evelyn_hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 29 May 2026 09:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fragmented stream + WS negotiation timeouts from Dedicated pool

Carlos — thanks for the quick flag and the captures. We're treating this as high priority. A few quick asks so we can triage in parallel:

- Can you confirm if the errors are concentrated on a single model/route or across several?
- Are clients using chunked transfer with SSE or raw WebSocket? (your trace hints at WS upgrades)
- Any repeating client IPs / connector IDs in the short window?

We're spinning up a focused incident thread and I will loop in Engineering and Support. In the meantime, I recommend switching that route to the standby fallback variant (model: gpt-small-v2-fallback) to reduce latency risk while we investigate. If you want we can also temporarily route traffic to our hosted pool in us-west-1 to buy time.

I'll update in 20–30 mins with initial findings.

Best,
Chloe Martin
Account Lead, Strategic Customers
Redwood Inference

Date: Fri, 29 May 2026 09:35:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Fragmented stream + WS negotiation timeouts from Dedicated pool

Team — escalating. Harmony (ded-78) is seeing chunked/fragmented payloads followed by an immediate WS close and reconnect storms. They report throughput down ~30% and p95 spike to ~1.4s. Packet capture attached.

What we know so far:
- Client-side shows WS upgrade succeeded then fragmented token frames, then 101 close.
- Errors appear across a small set of connector nodes (IDs in attached trace).
- No customer-initiated config changes.

Immediate asks: can infra confirm whether any kernel upgrades, NLB config changes, or proxy rotations happened between 08:50–09:10 PST? Sean — can you run an on-host trace for the connector instances and check websocket handshake latencies and chunk recomposition errors? Evelyn — please prep a quick summary for CS and leadership on impact and suggested mitigation.

I'll keep Harmony on the line and coordinate fallback routing if Engineering recommends it.

Chloe

Attachments: trace_log_20260529.txt (trace)

From: sean_gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: chloe_martin <chloe.martin@redwood.ai>, evelyn_hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>, jordan_blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 29 May 2026 10:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Fragmented stream + WS negotiation timeouts from Dedicated pool

Quick update from infra side after initial triage:

- No rolling kernel or NLB changes in the window.
- We observed elevated packet retransmits and TCP out-of-order segments between the connector tier and the serving nodes for the ded-78 affinity set starting ~09:03 PST. That aligns with the p95 jump.
- The WebSocket frames show correct upgrade sequences but partial application-level frames arriving fragmented (we see chunk seq numbers that don't complete) which causes our chunk-assembler to time out and close the socket.
- Early hypothesis: intermittent MTU blackholes or a misconfigured intermediate NAT translation causing segmentation of application frames.

Action items I'm executing now:
1) Spin a temporary route to the hosted us-west-1 pool for traffic from the affected connector IDs (reduces blast radius).
2) Increase chunk-assembler timeout to 3s for the ded-78 pool to reduce immediate closes (low-risk config change).
3) Request packet capture from the cloud provider on the affected fabric lanes (INF-9271).

I'll post the change window and rollback plan in INF-9271; expect the temporary mitigation in ~12 minutes. If mitigation reduces errors, we'll coordinate a postmortem with Harmony.

-sean
Sean Gallagher
Sr. Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference

Date: Fri, 29 May 2026 10:21:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fragmented stream + WS negotiation timeouts from Dedicated pool

Carlos — quick operational update:

- We routed traffic from the affected connector IDs to our hosted us-west-1 pool at 10:12 PST. Early telemetry shows error rate dropped from 5.2% -> 0.6% and p95 latency returned toward baseline.
- We also bumped the chunk assembler timeout to 3s in ded-78 at 10:10 PST; that reduced immediate closes while we wait on the provider capture.
- Engineering requested provider-side captures (INF-9271) and we are coordinating with them.

Next steps:
- If your team is comfortable, keep traffic on the hosted us-west-1 pool while we validate provider captures and root cause.
- We'll follow up with a targeted postmortem and permanent remediation (either path MTU enforcement or proxy-level reassembly fix) within 72 hours.

I know this impacted your SLAs — Evelyn is preparing a customer impact summary and proposed account-level credits if required. We appreciate your patience; we have leadership visibility on this and will keep you updated hourly until resolved.

Best,
Chloe Martin
Account Lead, Strategic Customers
Redwood Inference

I'll leave this open for the postmortem. Thanks again to you and the infra team for the quick work.
